title: Unpack One Sentence
tag: One classroom move, under three minutes, for the teacher who teaches content, not English.

beats.say: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move three: unpack one sentence.

chunks.text: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move three: unpack one sentence.

beats.say: Your Progressing students, the level threes and fours, are fine in discussion. Then you assign four pages of the textbook and they come back with nothing. The page didn't beat them. One sentence on it did.

chunks.text: Your Progressing students, the level threes and fours, are fine in discussion.
Then you assign four pages of the textbook and they come back with nothing. The page didn't beat them.
One sentence on it did.

a: During photosynthesis, energy from sunlight is used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
beats.say: Here's a real one. During photosynthesis, energy from sunlight is used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. One sentence. Five things happening. Passive voice. The subject, plants, buried in the middle.

chunks.text: Here's a real one.
During photosynthesis, energy from sunlight is used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
One sentence. Five things happening. Passive voice. The subject, plants, buried in the middle.

beats.say: The move: pick that sentence on purpose, before class, and take it apart on the board with the students. Ask the questions a reader asks.

chunks.text: The move: pick that sentence on purpose, before class, and take it apart on the board with the students.
Ask the questions a reader asks.

beats.say: Who does it? Plants. Not energy — energy is used by plants. Plants do it.

chunks.text: Who does it? Plants. Not energy — energy is used by plants. Plants do it.

beats.say: Does what? Convert. Change one thing into another.

chunks.text: Does what? Convert. Change one thing into another.

a: Converts what → into what? → CO₂ + water → glucose + oxygen
beats.say: Converts what into what? Carbon dioxide and water, into glucose and oxygen.

chunks.text: Converts what into what? Carbon dioxide and water, into glucose and oxygen.

beats.say: Using what? Energy from sunlight. Now every piece has a job.

chunks.text: Using what? Energy from sunlight. Now every piece has a job.

a: They convert carbon dioxide and water.
beats.say: Then rewrite it together as three short sentences. Plants use energy from sunlight. They convert carbon dioxide and water. They make glucose and oxygen. Same science. Three sentences a level two can read and a level four can now see inside of.

chunks.text: Then rewrite it together as three short sentences. Plants use energy from sunlight.
They convert carbon dioxide and water. They make glucose and oxygen. Same science.
Three sentences a level two can read and a level four can now see inside of.

beats.say: That's three minutes of class. And you didn't just help the English learners — you taught every student in the room how to read a science sentence, which nobody else is teaching them.

chunks.text: That's three minutes of class.
And you didn't just help the English learners — you taught every student in the room how to read a science sentence, which nobody else is teaching them.

a: Who? Does what? To what? Using what?
Let students do the next one
beats.say: Make it a habit. One sentence a day — the one you know will stop them. Pick it before class. Ask the same four questions every time: who, does what, to what, using what. Rewrite it short. After two weeks, hand the next sentence to a pair of students and let them unpack it.
